chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Ismāʿīl ibn al-Faḍl, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who travels from one land to another, and he only stops at his villages and his estate. He said: When you arrive at your villages and your estate, then perform the salat (prayer) in full; but when you are in other than your land, then shorten it.

key_terms.أَرْضِكَ: your land; one’s own place or territory
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer); the prescribed ritual prayer
key_terms.سَافَرَ: traveled; undertook a journey from one place to another
key_terms.ضَيْعَتَكَ: your estate; landed property or agricultural holding
key_terms.فَأَتِمَّ: then complete; perform in full without shortening
key_terms.فَقَصِّرْ: then shorten; perform the shortened traveler’s salat (prayer)
key_terms.قُرَاكَ: your villages; the settlements belonging to or associated with the person

ai.seo_question: When should a traveler perform salat (prayer) in full or shortened at his own village or estate?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the traveler’s salat (prayer) when passing through or staying at his own villages and estate. The Imam عليه السلام states that in one's own property or home land the salat (prayer) is to be performed in full, while outside one's land it is shortened.
